determination_context.original_question: Can stewardship controls detect drift? YES. Can they prevent/respond effectively? NOT YET. (S216: 30/100, INTERVENTION REQUIRED)
determination_context.s217_s219_response: S217-S219 provide complete remediation plans that close every gap S213-S216 identified. The plans are comprehensive, dependency-mapped, batch-gated, and verification-gated. BUT — they are PLANS, not executed remediations. The framework on paper can now detect, contain, and recover from all 6 drift categories. The framework in code still has the same vulnerabilities S213 found.
determination_context.key_tension: S220 must determine whether the existence of complete, verified remediation plans constitutes sufficient stewardship to re-certify — or whether the plans must be executed first.

domains.rationale: S208's 6 frozen principles are reaffirmed and strengthened by S217-S219 plans. No principle is weakened. P2 (Scan Once, Consume Many) gains cross-tool reconciliation gate. P6 (Traceability Everywhere) gains automated count-delta validation and T0→Tend verification. Principles are no longer aspirational — they have concrete enforcement mechanisms defined.

S217 defines exact single-owner assignments for all 6 entity classes, derivative registry headers, cross-registry T0 reconciliation, and Rule 7 BLOCK for new competing registries. The plan is complete. BUT — 5/6 registries currently have duplicate ownership. The S210→S214 regression demonstrates that designed authority chains without enforcement WILL diverge. Score reflects plan quality, not current state.

S218 defines complete D→C→R→P chains for all 6 categories. Every S213 undetected scenario (Shadow Queues, Manual Workarounds, Untracked Artifacts) now has a detection mechanism. Containment and recovery procedures are defined for every category. BUT — response quality is theoretical. S213's mean response quality was 1.67/5 with live scenarios. The playbook must be tested against live drift before this score can exceed 80.

S219 defines execution plans for the 3 highest-priority items with per-batch verification gates. TD-001 (58 Certified items, learner-safety HIGH) and TD-002 (39 Certified items, learner-safety HIGH) have concrete batch plans. TD-005 (DL-012 clones) escalated to this board for authorization. BUT — zero items have been remediated by these plans. The 2 highest learner-safety risks remain open. Score reflects plan completeness + governance readiness, not debt reduction.

Framework v2 is content-agnostic (S208 Board D confirmed). The governance guard, identity model, and defect enforcement apply to Part 2 without modification. S218 adds Part 2-ready SOURCE_FILE_RE extension to governance guard (S216 item 8). Minor improvement — Part 2 was already architecturally aligned.

May Admin was already 93/100 at S208 (Board E). S217-S219 plans do not directly affect May Admin operations. The 3 operational gaps identified at S208 (challenge triage 34%, student data zero, session mode unknowns) remain but are non-architectural. Score unchanged.

S218 defines complete operational resilience improvements: T0→Tmid→Tend checkpoint extensions, governance-critical file hash monitoring, backup enforcement, count-delta validation. S216 items 2-4, 9-11 addressed. BUT — DL-019 concurrent-write vulnerability not resolved in plans. Bash bypasses not prevented (OS-level limitation). Stale reference documents not yet updated. Score reflects plan quality.

overall.delta_from_s216: +35 (plan quality only — no content remediation executed)

determination_rationale:
S217-S219 provide comprehensive, dependency-mapped, batch-gated, verification-gated remediation plans that close every gap S213-S216 identified. The plans are complete, internally consistent, and consistent with S208's frozen architectural principles. No principle is violated. No plan introduces new risk. Every plan includes stop conditions and rollback procedures.

BUT — the plans are not yet executed. The 58 Certified Pack A items with DL-016 remain in the learner pool. The 39 Certified Domain F items with empty distractor slots remain undelivered. The 5/6 registries with duplicate ownership remain unresolved. The 3 undetected drift scenarios remain undetectable in live code.

The S220 Re-Certification Board CANNOT issue 'STEWARDSHIP RECERTIFIED' because the remediation has not been tested against live drift. But it CAN certify that the remediation architecture is complete and correct — moving the state from INTERVENTION REQUIRED (30/100) to STABLE (65/100) with a clear path to RECERTIFIED (90/100) upon execution.

This determination follows the same logic as S208: CONTINUE STEWARDSHIP was issued based on architectural completeness, not operational proof. S217-S219 provide architectural completeness for the response layer that S208 provided for the detection layer.
